issues.description: SealSaloon.orderMeal has conflicting return types: the UML/problem statement specifies `orderMeal(Meal): void`, but the solution implements `public boolean orderMeal(Meal meal)`. Students following the statement will implement a void method and may fail compilation/tests expecting the solution's boolean signature (or vice versa).
issues.suggestedFix: Make all artifacts and tests agree on the API. Preferred: change the solution to `public void orderMeal(Meal meal)` and remove boolean returns. If a success flag is intended, update the UML/problem statement to `orderMeal(Meal): boolean` and adapt tests accordingly.

issues.description: The exercise contradicts itself about whether SealSaloon.stock is instance-level or shared: it first states 'a final Stock stock' (instance field, read-only after construction), but later explicitly requires `stock` to be static (shared across all SealSaloon instances). This makes it unclear whether students should implement `private final Stock stock` or `private static final Stock stock` (the solution uses `private static final Stock stock`).
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the spec/UML inconsistency by choosing one model and applying it everywhere (statement, UML, tests, sample code). Either: (A) instance field `private final Stock stock` and make related methods instance methods, or (B) shared field `private static final Stock stock` and update the UML/earlier text to explicitly state it is static.

issues.description: Stock exposes a public mutator `setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[])` in the template/solution, but the UML/spec for Stock does not include this method. This allows bypassing the intended stock-management API (add/take/addToStockIngredients/emptyStock) and can mislead students about the required/allowed interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove `setStockIngredients(...)` from template/solution to match the UML (preferred for encapsulation), or add this method to the UML/spec and clarify it is intended only for testing/setup.
